root_cause.text: The rtl8723bs rtw_mlme code subtracted fixed IE offsets from the unsigned `pnetwork->network.ie_length` in `rtw_is_desired_network()` without first validating that the buffer length was at least those offsets, causing unsigned underflow and invalid length values passed to IE parsing helpers.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds explicit checks `if (pnetwork->network.ie_length < _FIXED_IE_LENGTH_) return false;` and `if (pnetwork->network.ie_length < _BEACON_IE_OFFSET_) { bselected = false; }` immediately before calls that previously used `pnetwork->network.ie_length - _FIXED_IE_LENGTH_` and `pnetwork->network.ie_length - _BEACON_IE_OFFSET_`, and the commit/CVE text explicitly says the guards prevent “unsigned integer underflow.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a length check before parsing WPS IEs so malformed short IE data is rejected safely.
intent_record.what: Within the WIFI_UNDER_WPS branch of rtw_is_desired_network(), a new conditional was added to check whether pnetwork->network.ie_length is smaller than _FIXED_IE_LENGTH_, and if so the function now immediately returns false before calling rtw_get_wps_ie().
intent_record.how: This prevents computing and passing an invalid IE buffer range based on ies + _FIXED_IE_LENGTH_ and ie_length - _FIXED_IE_LENGTH_ when the available IE data is shorter than the fixed header size, avoiding out-of-bounds access and rejecting malformed or incomplete network entries during WPS scanning.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a length check before parsing WPA2 RSN IEs so truncated beacon data is safely rejected during desired-network selection.
intent_record.what: The change wraps the WPA2-PSK RSN IE lookup in an additional conditional that first checks whether pnetwork->network.ie_length is smaller than _BEACON_IE_OFFSET_. If it is, bselected is set to false directly; otherwise, the existing call to rtw_get_ie(...) using ies + _BEACON_IE_OFFSET_ and length (ie_length - _BEACON_IE_OFFSET_) is performed, and bselected is set based on whether a valid RSN IE is found.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the code from subtracting _BEACON_IE_OFFSET_ from an undersized ie_length and from scanning beacon IEs starting past the valid buffer range. As a result, malformed or too-short network IE data is rejected safely instead of potentially causing invalid length calculations or out-of-bounds access during WPA2-PSK network selection.
